g4ela-24-1-morphology: Last root review of the year. Port means carry. Rupt means break. Struct means build. Dict means say. They’ve been hiding in words all year. Ask what each word is doing: carrying, breaking, building, or saying. Then sew the patch.
g4ela-24-2-grammar: A prepositional phrase is a little package. It starts with a word like in, on, under, or through, and it ends with a noun. In the baggage car. Through the woods. Find the first word, then find the noun that closes the package.
g4ela-24-3-spelling: Here’s the whole year in four words. Running: double the last letter after a short vowel. Hoping: drop the silent e. Happiest and carried: change y to i. Look at the end of the base word first. It tells you which rule fires.
g4ela-24-4-grammar: Last grammar job: the editor’s cut. Some sentences pile up so many little phrases that the action gets buried. Keep the ones the reader needs. Cut the rest. Then read it out loud. You should hear the verb again.
